$schema.description: The JSON Schema of this file, for editors: a path relative to the file (e.g. ../schemas/bindings.schema.json, as 'stratarec schema --out schemas' writes them) or a URL. The engine ignores it: it is not part of the file's content id.

mode.description: Where the features come from: 'fetch' (default) from the connector, on every request or, with a 'cache', when the cache has no fresh value; 'local' from an in-process table that 'bootstrap' loads in the background, with no I/O on the request path; 'service' from the service named by 'service', asked once per request for the features of an entity with args. Settings of another mode are errors.

service.description: Mode service, required: the service, under 'services', that computes the features of an entity with args: called once per request with the arguments as its inputs, each feature's 'field' the output it reads. Its timeout_ms and cache are the service's.

connector.description: Mode fetch, required: connector type and version, e.g. 'memory@1'. Other members of the binding not listed here are the connector's own settings (e.g. 'data_file').

timeout_ms.description: Modes fetch and service: time limit of one connector call, in milliseconds (default 50). With a cache, the whole read of the keys a request misses (the distributed tier, then the connector) stays within it; for service, the whole call of the service (its cache, then its client), whose own timeout_ms applies within it.

max_batch.description: Mode fetch: maximum keys per connector call (default 1000); larger batches are split into the fewest calls, of even size (9 keys at most 4 a call go as 3, 3 and 3), sent concurrently. With a cache, also the keys per read of its distributed tier.

max_bytes.description: Mode local, required: the most memory each table of the source (one per entity) may take, as an integer and a unit B, KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB, e.g. "512MiB". A load that would exceed it fails and the plan is not served. (A cache's memory is 'cache.memory.max_bytes'.)

bootstrap.description: Mode local, required: the update source that loads the table in the background, e.g. { "source": "snapshot_files@1", "uri": "fixtures/item_snapshot" }. A plan is served once every table it reads has completed its first load.

source.description: Required: update-source type and version, e.g. 'snapshot_files@1'. The other members are the source's own settings, which the schema describes for each type of the binary that wrote it.

uri.description: The snapshot directory (holding snapshot.json) or the manifest itself: a path relative to the configuration directory, an absolute path, or a file:// URI.

reload.description: How often to look for a new snapshot, as an ISO 8601 duration such as PT1H, at most P49D; without it, the snapshot is loaded once.

cache.description: Mode fetch, optional: keeps what the connector returned for 'ttl_ms', in process ('memory'), in a store the deployment's instances share ('distributed'), or both, e.g. { "ttl_ms": 60000, "memory": { "max_bytes": "256MiB" } }.

ttl_ms.description: How long a value fetched from the origin (the connector, or the service) is served, in milliseconds: required with a tier. Each key's lifetime varies by ±10% with the key's hash, so values written together do not all expire together. A cache with no member at all, "cache": {}, keeps nothing: the reads of one request share a value (the features of the request's user, a call of a service about no items) and the next request asks the origin again.

stale_if_error_ms.description: How much longer (milliseconds, default 0) an expired value may be served when the origin fails or times out; its readers are then Degraded.

version.description: Names what the cached values come from, e.g. "3". Without it the cache follows the configuration: a change of the connector or client, or of its own settings, starts the cache anew, since other settings may give other values. With it the cache follows this name instead: the values are kept across such changes, until you change the name. Changing ttl_ms, stale_if_error_ms, timeouts, max_bytes or the distributed store never starts it anew. Letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 64.

memory.description: The in-process tier: { "max_bytes": "256MiB" }. Hits take no I/O; each instance has its own. Worth it for keys many requests share (items); for keys of one user on a deployment of many instances, 'distributed' alone saves the memory.

max_bytes.description: Required: the most memory the tier's table may take (for a source, each of its entities' tables), as an integer and a unit B, KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB, e.g. "64MiB". A table that reaches it drops expired records first, then favors retaining recently read records.

distributed.description: The tier the deployment's instances share, read when the in-process tier (if any) has no fresh value, before the origin, e.g. { "store": "redis@1", "endpoint": "cache.internal:6379" }. Only an optimisation: when it fails or is slow, the keys go to the origin.

store.description: Required: store type and version, e.g. 'redis@1'. The other members are the store's own settings, which the schema describes for each type of the binary that wrote it.

timeout_ms.description: The longest a request waits for one read of the distributed cache, in milliseconds (default: half the source's or the service's timeout_ms; required for a service without one); always within that timeout_ms, so the origin keeps the rest of it.

endpoint.description: The server as host:port, e.g. redis.internal:6379; for a cluster, any of its nodes.

key_prefix.description: What every key starts with (default stratarec:), so that services sharing a server keep apart.

user.description: The ACL user to authenticate as.

password.description: The password, as a reference to the host's secret store (secret://name), resolved at load.

database.description: The database number (default 0; a cluster has only 0).

data.description: The records, by entity key: { "10042": { "i_clk_7d": 12.0 } }; for a key of several parts, one object level per part in the entity's key order, e.g. item, then country, then fields. Not with data_file; without either, there are none.

data_file.description: A JSON file of the records, as data holds them: a path relative to the configuration directory, an absolute path or a file:// URI.

latency_ms.description: Simulated latency of every fetch, in milliseconds (default 0).

services.description: The services the pipeline calls, by logical name: model servers, recall sources, any external service. A model operator's model and a recall's sources name them.

client.description: Required: client type and version, e.g. 'linear@1' or 'random@1' for a model, 'memory_list@1' for a recall source. The other members are the client's own settings, which the schema describes for each type of the binary that wrote it.

timeout_ms.description: Time limit of one call to the client, in milliseconds. The node's deadline bounds the call too, and alone without it.

cache.description: Caches the service's answers, e.g. { "ttl_ms": 60000, "memory": { "max_bytes": "64MiB" } }: a call about no items whole, one about items item by item (the items a call misses go to the service in one call). Keyed by the service version, the outputs read and the inputs, not by the request's seed: a service that samples by the seed reuses one answer for ttl_ms.

ttl_ms.description: How long a value fetched from the origin (the connector, or the service) is served, in milliseconds: required with a tier. Each key's lifetime varies by ±10% with the key's hash, so values written together do not all expire together. A cache with no member at all, "cache": {}, keeps nothing: the reads of one request share a value (the features of the request's user, a call of a service about no items) and the next request asks the origin again.

store.description: Required: store type and version, e.g. 'redis@1'. The other members are the store's own settings, which the schema describes for each type of the binary that wrote it.

timeout_ms.description: The longest a request waits for one read of the distributed cache, in milliseconds (default: half the source's or the service's timeout_ms; required for a service without one); always within that timeout_ms, so the origin keeps the rest of it.

endpoint.description: The server as host:port, e.g. redis.internal:6379; for a cluster, any of its nodes.

key_prefix.description: What every key starts with (default stratarec:), so that services sharing a server keep apart.

user.description: The ACL user to authenticate as.

password.description: The password, as a reference to the host's secret store (secret://name), resolved at load.

database.description: The database number (default 0; a cluster has only 0).

inputs.description: The model's text input names, as its signature declares them (the prompts the calling operator renders), e.g. ["system", "user"]: at least one, each once.

outputs.description: Each text output and the text every call answers, e.g. { "answer": "[3, 1, 2]" }: at least one.
The model's outputs by name, each a weighted sum of its inputs, e.g. { "p_click": { "bias": -2.0, "weights": { "smoothed_ctr": 8.0 }, "activation": "sigmoid" } }.

weights.description: Input name to its weight. The model's inputs are the names the outputs weigh.

versions.description: The model versions a call may ask for, e.g. ["v12", "v13"]; any version when omitted.

latency_ms.description: Simulated latency of every call, in milliseconds (default 0).

data_file.description: A JSON file of the other members: a path relative to the configuration directory, an absolute path or a file:// URI. A member the binding has too is the binding's.

items.description: The list, best first: ids (strings or int64s) or { "id": …, "score": … } objects; scores default to a descending ramp.

by_input.description: The input of the call whose value picks the list of lists a call gets: a value the recall node's queries sends, e.g. "queries": { "popular": { "user_id": "ctx.request.user_id" } }.

lists.description: A list per value of by_input, each like items; "*" is the list of every other value.

latency_ms.description: Simulated latency of every retrieval, in milliseconds (default 0).

query.description: The query value holding the query vector (MultiSourceRecall@1's queries), such as "user_embedding": a list of floats of the items' vectors' length.

min_score.description: The least score an item is returned with; without it, every item may be.

data_file.description: A JSON file of the items ({ "items": [ … ] }): a path relative to the configuration directory, an absolute path or a file:// URI. Items in the binding are the binding's.

latency_ms.description: Simulated latency of every retrieval, in milliseconds (default 0).

items.description: The indexed items, each { "id": …, "vector": [ … ] }; every vector of one length.

id.description: The candidate's id: a string or an int64.

vector.description: Its vector, scored by its dot product with the query vector.

inputs.description: The inputs of the model it stands in for, as the model declares them: their names, each a float32 tensor of shape [-1] (["smoothed_ctr", "log_followers"]), or each name mapped to its tensor ({ "item_id": { "type": "int64", "shape": [-1, 2] } }). At least one, each once.

outputs.description: The outputs, as the model declares them: their names, each a float32 tensor of shape [-1] (["p_click"]), or each name mapped to its shape and, for a float64 score, its type ({ "p_first": { "shape": [-1] }, "p_like": { "type": "float64", "shape": [-1] } }). At least one, each once.

seed.description: A fixed seed instead of the call's (ctx.request.seed): every request gets the same scores.

pipelines.description: What this environment gives the calls of a pipeline, by the called pipeline's id: where their cached results are kept, e.g. { "rank": { "cache": { "distributed": { "store": "redis@1", "endpoint": "cache.internal:6379", "timeout_ms": 15 } } } }. A node that calls the pipeline says whether its calls are cached and for how long (the 'cache' of its config).

cache.description: Where the results of the pipeline's cached calls are kept: 'memory', 'distributed' or both, as for a source's or a service's cache. How long a result is served is not said here: each node that calls the pipeline says it for its own calls ('cache' in the node's config: ttl_ms, stale_if_error_ms, version).

memory.description: The in-process tier: { "max_bytes": "64MiB" }. Each instance has its own: results keyed by a user are rarely found again on a deployment of many instances, for which 'distributed' is the tier to have.

max_bytes.description: Required: the most memory the tier's table may take (for a source, each of its entities' tables), as an integer and a unit B, KiB, MiB, GiB or TiB, e.g. "64MiB". A table that reaches it drops expired records first, then favors retaining recently read records.

distributed.description: The tier the deployment's instances share, e.g. { "store": "redis@1", "endpoint": "cache.internal:6379", "timeout_ms": 15 }. Its timeout_ms is required: a pipeline has no timeout of its own to take half of. When it fails or is slow, the pipeline runs.

store.description: Required: store type and version, e.g. 'redis@1'. The other members are the store's own settings, which the schema describes for each type of the binary that wrote it.

timeout_ms.description: The longest a request waits for one read of the distributed cache, in milliseconds (default: half the source's or the service's timeout_ms; required for a service without one); always within that timeout_ms, so the origin keeps the rest of it.

endpoint.description: The server as host:port, e.g. redis.internal:6379; for a cluster, any of its nodes.

key_prefix.description: What every key starts with (default stratarec:), so that services sharing a server keep apart.

user.description: The ACL user to authenticate as.

password.description: The password, as a reference to the host's secret store (secret://name), resolved at load.

database.description: The database number (default 0; a cluster has only 0).
